530	**GUIDELINES FOR MOTIONS SEEKING ENTRY OF FINAL DECREE IN CHAPTER 11 CASES**
531	
532	Office of the United States Trustee 620 SW Main Street, Suite 213 Portland, OR 97205
533	
534	**Revised January 2024**
535	
536	These Guidelines are for informational purposes and are intended to assist practitioners in preparing motions for entry of a final decree under 11 U.S.C. § 350(a) and Fed. R. Bankr. P. 3022. Compliance with these Guidelines does not guarantee the United States Trustee\'s consent to case closure.
537	
538	**[I. Purpose and Legal Framework]{.underline}**
539	
540	The purpose of these Guidelines is to establish uniform requirements for motions seeking entry of a final decree in Chapter 11 cases pending in the United States Bankruptcy Courts for the District of Oregon and the District of Alaska, which together comprise Region 18 of the United States Trustee Program.
541	
542	The entry of a final decree and the closing of a Chapter 11 case are governed by the following statutory and procedural provisions:
543	
544	> • **11 U.S.C. § 350(a):** \"After an estate is fully administered and the court has discharged the trustee, the court shall close the case.\"
545	>
546	> • **Fed. R. Bankr. P. 3022:** \"After an estate is fully administered in a chapter 11 reorganization case, the court, on its own motion or on motion of a party in interest, shall enter a final decree closing the case.\"
547	
548	The Advisory Committee Note to Rule 3022 sets forth a non-exhaustive list of factors relevant to determining whether an estate has been fully administered and whether entry of a final decree is appropriate. These factors form the analytical framework that the United States Trustee applies when reviewing final decree motions.
549	
550	The United States Trustee has an independent obligation under 28 U.S.C. § 586(a)(3) to supervise the administration of cases and trustees in cases filed under Title 11 of the United States Code. Pursuant to this statutory mandate, the United States Trustee will review all motions for entry of a final decree filed in Chapter 11 cases within Region 18. The United States Trustee will file a response to any final decree motion within twenty-one (21) days of service and may consent, object, or take no position with respect to the relief requested. Movants should serve the motion on the United States Trustee at the following address: Office of the United States Trustee, 620 SW Main Street, Suite 213, Portland, OR 97205.
551	
552	**[II. When to File a Final Decree Motion]{.underline}**
553	
554	A motion for entry of a final decree should not be filed until the case has been \"fully administered\" as contemplated by 11 U.S.C. § 350(a) and Fed. R. Bankr. P. 3022. The determination of whether a case has been fully administered is a factual inquiry informed by the totality of the circumstances. In evaluating whether a case is ripe for closure, the United States Trustee will consider the factors identified in the Advisory Committee Note to Rule 3022, which include the following:
555	
556	1\. Whether the order confirming the plan has become final;
557	
558	2\. Whether the plan has been substantially consummated as defined by 11 U.S.C. § 1101(2);
559	
560	3\. Whether deposits required by the plan have been distributed;
561	
562	4\. Whether property proposed by the plan to be transferred has been transferred;
563	
564	5\. Whether the debtor or the successor of the debtor under the plan has assumed the business or the management of property dealt with by the plan;
565	
566	6\. Whether payments under the plan have commenced;
567	
568	7\. Whether all motions, contested matters, and adversary proceedings have been finally resolved;
569	
570	8\. Whether all administrative claims, including applications for compensation and reimbursement of expenses under 11 U.S.C. §§ 330 and 331, have been resolved and paid; and
571	
572	9\. Whether the United States Trustee has filed a final report or has no objection to case closure.
573	
574	The United States Trustee generally expects that a motion for entry of a final decree will not be filed until after (a) the plan has been substantially consummated, and (b) substantially all post-confirmation matters --- including distributions, claims resolution, and administrative and fiduciary matters --- have been completed or are on the verge of completion.
575	
576	Movants are encouraged to file the motion for entry of a final decree at least twenty-eight (28) days before the requested hearing date to allow the United States Trustee adequate time to review the motion and all supporting materials and to file a response within the twenty-one (21) day response period established by these Guidelines.
577	
578	**[III. Required Certifications and Representations]{.underline}**
579	
580	The motion for entry of a final decree must include each of the following certifications or representations, supported by specific factual detail. Conclusory statements that a particular requirement has been satisfied are insufficient. The movant should provide dates, amounts, docket references, and other verifiable information wherever possible.
581	
582	**A. Quarterly Fee Certification (28 U.S.C. § 1930(a)(6))**
583	
584	The movant must certify that all quarterly fees due under 28 U.S.C. § 1930(a)(6) have been paid in full through the most recent quarter. Quarterly fees must be current as of the date of filing of the motion. Fees that have accrued for the current quarter but are not yet due must be addressed in the motion.
585	
586	The movant must represent that it will pay all quarterly fees through and including the quarter in which the final decree is entered and the case is closed. Section 1930(a)(6) provides that quarterly fees accrue based on disbursements made during each calendar quarter and must be paid for each quarter (or portion thereof) during which the case remains open, until the case is closed, dismissed, or converted.
587	
588	If fees for the current quarter have accrued but are not yet paid as of the filing date of the motion, the motion must include one of the following: (a) proof of payment made prior to filing; (b) a commitment to pay all outstanding quarterly fees before the hearing date; or (c) a request that entry of the final decree be conditioned upon payment of all outstanding quarterly fees, including fees for the quarter in which the case is closed.
589	
590	The United States Trustee will object to entry of a final decree if quarterly fees are not current or if the motion fails to include an adequate undertaking to pay all fees through case closure. The movant should include the date and amount of the most recent quarterly fee payment and confirm that such payment has been verified against the records maintained by the United States Trustee.
591	
592	**B. Post-Confirmation Operating Reports**
593	
594	The movant must certify that all post-confirmation operating reports --- whether required on a monthly basis or on such other schedule as the Court or the United States Trustee has directed --- have been filed through the most recent reporting period. All monthly operating reports must be filed and current before the United States Trustee will consent to entry of a final decree. If the most recent operating report has not yet been filed because it is not yet due, the movant must commit to filing all outstanding reports --- including a final operating report covering the period through the date of case closure --- before or contemporaneously with entry of the final decree.
595	
596	If the motion is filed before the most recent report\'s due date, the motion must acknowledge the outstanding reporting obligation and provide a specific commitment, with a date certain, by which the outstanding report and any final operating report will be filed and served. The United States Trustee may require a final operating report that covers the period from the date of the last filed report through the date of case closure, reflecting all final disbursements and receipts of the estate or the reorganized debtor.
597	
598	Failure to file all required operating reports, including any final report covering the period through case closure, will result in an objection by the United States Trustee.
599	
600	**C. Resolution of All Professional Fee Applications**
601	
602	The movant must certify that all applications for compensation and reimbursement of expenses under 11 U.S.C. §§ 330 and 331 have been filed, heard, and either allowed or disallowed by the Court, and that all allowed professional fees and expenses have been paid in full. The certification should identify by docket number each final fee application filed, the amount requested, the amount allowed, and the date of payment.
603	
604	If any professional --- including a plan administrator, disbursing agent, or other post-confirmation fiduciary --- will continue to incur fees or expenses after the motion is filed but before the case is closed, the motion must address how such fees will be resolved. Appropriate mechanisms include, by way of example, payment by the reorganized debtor outside of the bankruptcy case pursuant to the terms of the confirmed plan, or establishment and maintenance of a final fee reserve sufficient to cover anticipated remaining professional obligations.
605	
606	**D. Resolution of All Adversary Proceedings, Contested Matters, and Motions**
607	
608	The movant must certify that all adversary proceedings, contested matters, and pending motions have been fully and finally resolved. The certification should identify each adversary proceeding by case number, each contested matter by docket number, and state the manner and date of resolution (e.g., final order, dismissal, settlement approval).
609	
610	If any adversary proceeding or contested matter remains pending as of the filing date of the motion, the movant must disclose the nature and status of each such matter and explain why case closure is nonetheless appropriate. The United States Trustee generally will not consent to entry of a final decree while adversary proceedings remain pending, unless the movant demonstrates that all remaining matters are ministerial or are scheduled for imminent resolution.
611	
612	If a settlement has been reached in any pending matter but has not yet been approved by the Court, the movant must identify the pending settlement approval motion by docket number, the hearing date, and the anticipated timeline for final resolution. The United States Trustee may condition its consent to case closure on the Court\'s approval of any pending settlement.
613	
614	**E. Completion of All Plan Distributions**
615	
616	The movant must certify that all distributions required under the confirmed plan have been made to all classes of creditors and interest holders entitled to receive distributions, or that any remaining distributions are purely ministerial in nature and will be completed before or upon entry of the final decree. The certification should identify the total amount distributed under the plan, the date of the most recent distribution, and the nature of any remaining distributions.
617	
618	If a disputed claims reserve was established under the plan, the movant must certify that all disputed claims have been resolved by final order of the Court and that all reserve funds have been distributed to claimants or returned to the appropriate parties in accordance with the plan\'s distribution and surplus provisions. The movant must also certify that all avoidance action recoveries have been or will be distributed in accordance with the plan\'s provisions governing such recoveries.
619	
620	**F. Filing of Tax Returns**
621	
622	The movant must certify that all required federal, state, and local tax returns for the debtor and for the bankruptcy estate (to the extent the estate constitutes a separate taxable entity) have been filed through all relevant tax periods. This certification should specifically address income tax returns, employment tax returns, sales and use tax returns, and any other returns required by applicable taxing authorities.
623	
624	The movant should reference 11 U.S.C. § 346 and applicable Internal Revenue Service guidance regarding the filing obligations of a debtor in a Chapter 11 case and the treatment of the bankruptcy estate as a separate taxable entity. The certification should cover all periods from the petition date through the most recently completed tax period, including any short-year returns required upon confirmation of the plan or the effective date of the plan.
625	
626	If the estate was treated as a separate taxable entity during any period, the movant must certify that all returns for that entity have been filed and are current. The United States Trustee may request confirmation from the Internal Revenue Service and applicable state taxing authorities that all returns have been filed. Failure to file required tax returns may result in an objection to case closure.
627	
628	**G. Plan Administrator or Trustee Final Report**
629	
630	If a plan administrator, disbursing agent, liquidating trustee, or other post-confirmation fiduciary was appointed under the confirmed plan, the movant must certify that such party has filed a final report with the Court. The final report must detail all distributions made, all claims resolved (with disposition), all funds received and disbursed, and the status of any remaining matters. The final report should be filed with the Court and served upon the United States Trustee before or contemporaneously with the filing of the final decree motion so that the United States Trustee may review it in connection with its evaluation of the motion.
631	
632	**[IV. Motion Format and Content Requirements]{.underline}**
633	
634	The motion for entry of a final decree must include the following components:
635	
636	1\. **Full caption** with the case number, chapter designation, and the name of the assigned bankruptcy judge;
637	
638	2\. **Identification of the movant** and a statement of its relationship to the case (e.g., reorganized debtor, plan administrator, liquidating trustee);
639	
640	3\. **Concise statement of the relief requested**, specifying entry of a final decree closing the case;
641	
642	4\. **Factual background section** summarizing the procedural and substantive history of the case, including the petition date, plan confirmation date, effective date, and key post-confirmation events and milestones;
643	
644	5\. **Legal standard section** citing 11 U.S.C. § 350(a), Fed. R. Bankr. P. 3022, and the Advisory Committee Note factors;
645	
646	6\. **Argument section** addressing each Advisory Committee Note factor with specific factual support demonstrating that the case has been fully administered;
647	
648	7\. **Certification section** specifically addressing each of the certifications required by Section III of these Guidelines;
649	
650	8\. **Prayer for relief** requesting entry of the final decree and such other relief as the Court deems just and proper;
651	
652	9\. **Proposed form of order**; and
653	
654	10\. **Certificate of service** demonstrating proper service on the United States Trustee, all parties who have filed a notice of appearance or request for service in the case, and any parties with continuing interests under the plan (e.g., indenture trustees, plan administrators, exit facility lenders, members of creditors\' committees that have not been dissolved).
655	
656	The proposed order submitted with the motion should include:
657	
658	> • A decretal paragraph directing entry of a final decree and the administrative closing of the case;
659	>
660	> • Any conditions precedent to case closure (e.g., payment of remaining quarterly fees, filing of a final operating report);
661	>
662	> • A provision addressing the Court\'s retention of jurisdiction for post-closure matters, including but not limited to plan enforcement, interpretation of the confirmation order, resolution of disputes arising under the plan, and reopening of the case under 11 U.S.C. § 350(b); and
663	>
664	> • A provision confirming that the discharge granted under 11 U.S.C. § 1141(d) and any injunctions contained in the confirmation order and the plan shall survive case closure and remain in full force and effect.
665	
666	**[V. U.S. Trustee Review and Response Procedures]{.underline}**
667	
668	Upon receipt of a properly served motion for entry of a final decree, the United States Trustee will review the motion and all supporting materials and will file a response within twenty-one (21) days of service. The United States Trustee may take one of the following positions:
669	
670	> • **Statement of No Objection:** If the United States Trustee determines that all requirements set forth in these Guidelines and applicable law have been satisfied, the United States Trustee will file a statement indicating that it has no objection to entry of the final decree.
671	>
672	> • **Limited Objection:** If the United States Trustee identifies specific, curable deficiencies --- such as unpaid quarterly fees, unfiled operating reports, pending adversary proceedings, or outstanding tax returns --- the United States Trustee will file a limited objection identifying each deficiency with specificity.
673	>
674	> • **Full Objection:** If the United States Trustee determines that the case has not been fully administered and that the identified deficiencies are not merely ministerial or readily curable, the United States Trustee will file an objection to the motion in its entirety.
675	
676	If the United States Trustee files a limited objection identifying specific deficiencies, the movant may cure the deficiencies and file a supplemental certification with the Court and serve a copy on the United States Trustee. Upon receipt of the supplemental certification and verification that all deficiencies have been resolved, the United States Trustee will reconsider its position and file an amended response with the Court as appropriate.
677	
678	The United States Trustee strongly encourages movants and their counsel to contact the assigned United States Trustee attorney informally before filing the motion for entry of a final decree. Early communication allows the parties to identify and resolve potential issues in advance, which may expedite the case closure process and avoid unnecessary litigation. Inquiries may be directed to: Office of the United States Trustee, Region 18, 620 SW Main Street, Suite 213, Portland, OR 97205; Telephone: (503) 326-4000.
679	
680	**[VI. Checklist for Final Decree Motions (Chapter 11)]{.underline}**
681	
682	The following checklist is provided for the convenience of practitioners. Movants should verify that each item has been satisfied or adequately addressed in the motion before filing.
683	
684	> • Order confirming the plan has become final and non-appealable
685	>
686	> • Plan has been substantially consummated (11 U.S.C. § 1101(2))
687	>
688	> • All plan distributions completed (or remaining distributions are ministerial and will be completed before case closure)
689	>
690	> • Disputed claims reserve fully administered; surplus distributed or returned per plan terms
691	>
692	> • All avoidance action recoveries distributed per plan terms
693	>
694	> • All quarterly fees under 28 U.S.C. § 1930(a)(6) paid current, with adequate undertaking to pay through the quarter of case closure
695	>
696	> • All post-confirmation monthly operating reports filed current, with commitment to file final report covering the period through case closure
697	>
698	> • All professional fee applications under §§ 330 and 331 filed, heard, and allowed amounts paid in full
699	>
700	> • Ongoing professional or fiduciary compensation adequately addressed (e.g., plan administrator fees post-closure)
701	>
702	> • All adversary proceedings, contested matters, and pending motions fully resolved (or imminent resolution demonstrated with specificity)
703	>
704	> • All federal, state, and local tax returns filed current, including any short-year or separate estate returns
705	>
706	> • Plan administrator, disbursing agent, or liquidating trustee final report filed and served on U.S. Trustee
707	>
708	> • Proposed order includes jurisdiction retention language
709	>
710	> • Proposed order confirms survival of discharge under § 1141(d) and plan injunctions post-closure
711	>
712	> • Certificate of service demonstrates proper service on the United States Trustee and all required parties
713	
714	These Guidelines are issued by the Office of the United States Trustee for Region 18 and do not constitute legal advice. They are subject to revision without notice. Compliance with these Guidelines does not guarantee that the United States Trustee will consent to entry of a final decree in any particular case. Practitioners should consult the Bankruptcy Code, the Federal Rules of Bankruptcy Procedure, the Local Bankruptcy Rules for the District of Oregon and the District of Alaska, and applicable case law. All inquiries regarding these Guidelines should be directed to the Office of the United States Trustee, Region 18, 620 SW Main Street, Suite 213, Portland, OR 97205.
715	
716	Revision Date: January 2024

    l, r = t.rows[0].cells
    cell_text(l, ["In re:", "", "**CASCADIA TIMBER HOLDINGS, INC.,**", "an Oregon corporation,", "EIN 93-1284756,", "", "                                        *Debtor.*"])
    set_cell_border(l, right={"val":"single","sz":"6","color":"000000"}, bottom={"val":"single","sz":"6","color":"000000"})
    cell_text(r, ["   Case No. 22-30847-PCW", "", "   Chapter 11", "", "   Hon. Patricia C. Wellborne", "", ""] + ["   " + x for x in title])
    para(d, "", spacing=1.0, after=6)

def grid_table(d, header, rows, widths, size=10, bold_last=False):
    t = d.add_table(rows=1+len(rows), cols=len(header))
    t.style = "Table Grid"
    t.alignment = WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT.CENTER
    for i, h in enumerate(header):
        cell_text(t.rows[0].cells[i], ["**"+h+"**"], size=size)
        shd = OxmlElement("w:shd"); shd.set(qn("w:val"), "clear"); shd.set(qn("w:color"), "auto"); shd.set(qn("w:fill"), "D9D9D9")
        t.rows[0].cells[i]._tc.get_or_add_tcPr().append(shd)
    for ri, row in enumerate(rows):
        for ci, v in enumerate(row):
            txt = ("**"+v+"**") if (bold_last and ri == len(rows)-1 and v) else v
            cell_text(t.rows[ri+1].cells[ci], [txt], size=size)
    set_col_widths(t, widths)
    para(d, "", spacing=1.0, after=6)
    return t

heading(d, "A.\tLegal Standard", 2)
N("Section 350(a) provides: “After an estate is fully administered and the court has discharged the trustee, the court shall close the case.” 11 U.S.C. § 350(a). Bankruptcy Rule 3022 implements that directive in chapter 11 cases: once the estate is fully administered, the court, on its own or on the motion of a party in interest, must enter a final decree closing the case. Fed. R. Bankr. P. 3022. No trustee was appointed in this case, so no discharge of a trustee is required.")
N("Neither the Bankruptcy Code nor the Rules define “fully administered.” The Advisory Committee Note to the 1991 amendment of Rule 3022 identifies factors the court should consider, including: (1) whether the order confirming the plan has become final; (2) whether deposits required by the plan have been distributed; (3) whether the property proposed by the plan to be transferred has been transferred; (4) whether the debtor or the successor of the debtor under the plan has assumed the business or the management of the property dealt with by the plan; (5) whether payments under the plan have commenced; and (6) whether all motions, contested matters, and adversary proceedings have been finally resolved. Fed. R. Bankr. P. 3022 advisory committee’s note to 1991 amendment. The UST Guidelines add whether the plan has been substantially consummated under section 1101(2), whether administrative claims (including professional compensation) have been resolved and paid, and the U.S. Trustee’s position. UST Guidelines § II.")
N("These factors are guidelines, not a checklist; not every factor must be present, and the inquiry turns on the totality of the circumstances. *See, e.g.*, *In re Union Home & Indus., Inc.*, 375 B.R. 912, 916–17 (B.A.P. 10th Cir. 2007); *In re Gates Cmty. Chapel of Rochester, Inc.*, 212 B.R. 220, 224 (Bankr. W.D.N.Y. 1997); *In re Mold Makers, Inc.*, 124 B.R. 766, 768–69 (Bankr. N.D. Ill. 1990). The Advisory Committee Note emphasizes that entry of a final decree “should not be delayed solely because the payments required by the plan have not been completed,” and that the court should not keep a case open “only because of the possibility that the court’s jurisdiction may be invoked in the future.” Fed. R. Bankr. P. 3022 advisory committee’s note to 1991 amendment. A final decree does not deprive the court of jurisdiction to enforce or interpret its own orders, and the case may be reopened for cause under section 350(b). *Id.*; *see* 11 U.S.C. § 350(b). Courts thus regard a case as fully administered when the plan has been substantially consummated and the matters that remain are ministerial or are governed by the plan and can be carried out by the reorganized debtor without court supervision. *See In re Kliegl Bros. Universal Elec. Stage Lighting Co.*, 238 B.R. 531, 542 (Bankr. E.D.N.Y. 1999); *In re Federated Dep’t Stores, Inc.*, 43 F. App’x 820, 822–23 (6th Cir. 2002). [Cite-check; add controlling Ninth Circuit/District of Oregon authority if available.]")

para(d, "Cascadia Timber Holdings, Inc., the reorganized debtor (the “**Reorganized Debtor**” and, before the Effective Date, the “**Debtor**”) in the above-captioned chapter 11 case (the “**Chapter 11 Case**”), by and through its undersigned counsel, and with the support of Stonecreek Advisory Group, LLC, in its capacity as Plan Administrator (the “**Plan Administrator**”), hereby moves (this “**Motion**”) for entry of a final decree closing the Chapter 11 Case pursuant to section 350(a) of title 11 of the United States Code (the “**Bankruptcy Code**”) and Rule 3022 of the Federal Rules of Bankruptcy Procedure (the “**Bankruptcy Rules**”), substantially in the form of the proposed order filed herewith as **Exhibit 1** (the “**Proposed Final Decree**”). In support of this Motion, the Reorganized Debtor relies on the record of the Chapter 11 Case, including the Plan Administrator’s Final Status Report filed January 31, 2025 [Dkt. No. 501] (the “**Final Status Report**”), the Declaration of [__________], [title] of the Reorganized Debtor (the “**Debtor Declaration**”), and the Supplemental Declaration of Douglas R. Emmerich on behalf of the Plan Administrator (the “**PA Declaration**”), each filed contemporaneously herewith, and respectfully states as follows:")

heading(d, "PRELIMINARY STATEMENT")
N("This Chapter 11 Case has accomplished its purpose. The Court confirmed the Second Amended Joint Chapter 11 Plan of Reorganization of Cascadia Timber Holdings, Inc. (as confirmed, the “**Plan**”) [Dkt. No. 398] on November 9, 2023 [Dkt. No. 412] (the “**Confirmation Order**”). The Plan went effective on December 1, 2023 (the “**Effective Date**”), when the Plan Sponsor funded its $38.5 million new value contribution, the $55 million exit facility closed and funded, all estate property vested in the Reorganized Debtor, and Effective Date distributions were made. Since then, the Reorganized Debtor and the Plan Administrator have distributed approximately $110.4 million in cash and new secured notes to creditors, resolved every disputed claim, administered and closed the Disputed Claims Reserve, and obtained final allowance and payment of the estate professionals’ fees. The Reorganized Debtor operates all six of its sawmill facilities in the ordinary course, is current on its post-Effective Date obligations, and reports trailing twelve-month EBITDA of approximately $22.3 million.")
N("A small number of discrete, ministerial items remain, and the Reorganized Debtor discloses each of them candidly in Part II.E below: (a) the Court’s ruling on the pending motion to approve the $525,000 settlement of the sole remaining adversary proceeding [Dkt. No. 498], which is set for hearing on February 20, 2025, and the receipt and distribution of the resulting net proceeds to Class 4; (b) payment of the U.S. Trustee quarterly fees for the first quarter of 2025 and for the quarter in which the case is closed; (c) filing of the January 2025 and subsequent post-confirmation operating reports, including a final report through the closing date; (d) [final allowance of the remaining professional and Plan Administrator compensation for the pre-closing period;] and (e) filing of a supplemental final report by the Plan Administrator and written confirmation that IRS Claim No. 14 has been satisfied. None of these items requires continued estate administration of the type that justifies keeping a chapter 11 case open.")
N("Consistent with the Region 18 U.S. Trustee’s *Guidelines for Motions Seeking Entry of Final Decree in Chapter 11 Cases* (rev. Jan. 2024) (the “**UST Guidelines**”), which expressly contemplate that a final decree may be conditioned on payment of outstanding quarterly fees and the Court’s approval of a pending settlement, the Reorganized Debtor requests entry of a final decree that becomes effective upon the Reorganized Debtor’s filing of a certification that each of the Closing Conditions (defined below) has been satisfied, absent timely objection by the U.S. Trustee. Keeping the case open beyond that point would serve only to impose continuing quarterly fees and reporting costs on the Reorganized Debtor without any corresponding benefit to creditors.")

heading(d, "I.  JURISDICTION, VENUE, AND STATUTORY PREDICATES")
N("The Court has jurisdiction over this Motion under 28 U.S.C. §§ 157 and 1334. This is a core proceeding under 28 U.S.C. § 157(b)(2)(A) and (O). Venue is proper under 28 U.S.C. §§ 1408 and 1409.")
N("The Court expressly retained jurisdiction “to enter a final decree closing this case pursuant to 11 U.S.C. § 350(a) and Fed. R. Bankr. P. 3022.” Confirmation Order ¶ O(n); *see also* Plan § 12.1(k).")
N("The statutory and rule predicates for the relief requested are section 350(a) of the Bankruptcy Code, Bankruptcy Rule 3022, and [the applicable Local Bankruptcy Rules of this Court].")

heading(d, "A.\tThe Chapter 11 Case", 2)
N("The Debtor is an Oregon corporation (EIN 93-1284756) headquartered at 4200 Evergreen Industrial Parkway, Suite 300, Medford, Oregon 97501. It is a vertically integrated timber harvesting, sawmill, and engineered wood products company with six sawmill and processing facilities in Oregon and Washington and harvesting rights on approximately 340,000 acres of managed timberland. Before the petition it employed approximately 1,400 people and generated annual revenue of approximately $185 million.")
N("On March 14, 2022 (the “**Petition Date**”), the Debtor filed a voluntary petition for relief under chapter 11 of the Bankruptcy Code [Dkt. No. 1]. The Debtor’s schedules reflected assets of approximately $198.6 million and liabilities of approximately $247.3 million. No trustee or examiner was appointed. The Debtor operated its business and managed its property as a debtor in possession under sections 1107(a) and 1108 of the Bankruptcy Code until the Effective Date.")
N("On April 8, 2022, the U.S. Trustee appointed the Official Committee of Unsecured Creditors (the “**Committee**”) [Dkt. No. [28/38]], which retained Pendergrass & Hale LLP as counsel [Dkt. No. 42]. No. 15].")

heading(d, "IV.  BASIS FOR RELIEF")
heading(d, "A.\tLegal Standard", 2)
N("Section 350(a) provides: “After an estate is fully administered and the court has discharged the trustee, the court shall close the case.” 11 U.S.C. § 350(a). Bankruptcy Rule 3022 implements that directive in chapter 11 cases: once the estate is fully administered, the court, on its own or on the motion of a party in interest, must enter a final decree closing the case. Fed. R. Bankr. P. 3022. No trustee was appointed in this case, so no discharge of a trustee is required.")
N("Neither the Bankruptcy Code nor the Rules define “fully administered.” The Advisory Committee Note to the 1991 amendment of Rule 3022 identifies factors the court should consider, including: (1) whether the order confirming the plan has become final; (2) whether deposits required by the plan have been distributed; (3) whether the property proposed by the plan to be transferred has been transferred; (4) whether the debtor or the successor of the debtor under the plan has assumed the business or the management of the property dealt with by the plan; (5) whether payments under the plan have commenced; and (6) whether all motions, contested matters, and adversary proceedings have been finally resolved. Fed. R. Bankr. P. 3022 advisory committee’s note to 1991 amendment. The UST Guidelines add whether the plan has been substantially consummated under section 1101(2), whether administrative claims (including professional compensation) have been resolved and paid, and the U.S. Trustee’s position. UST Guidelines § II.")
N("These factors are guidelines, not a checklist; not every factor must be present, and the inquiry turns on the totality of the circumstances. *See, e.g.*, *In re Union Home & Indus., Inc.*, 375 B.R. 912, 916–17 (B.A.P. 10th Cir. 2007); *In re Gates Cmty. Chapel of Rochester, Inc.*, 212 B.R. 220, 224 (Bankr. W.D.N.Y. 1997); *In re Mold Makers, Inc.*, 124 B.R. 766, 768–69 (Bankr. N.D. Ill. 1990). The Advisory Committee Note emphasizes that entry of a final decree “should not be delayed solely because the payments required by the plan have not been completed,” and that the court should not keep a case open “only because of the possibility that the court’s jurisdiction may be invoked in the future.” Fed. R. Bankr. P. 3022 advisory committee’s note to 1991 amendment. A final decree does not deprive the court of jurisdiction to enforce or interpret its own orders, and the case may be reopened for cause under section 350(b). *Id.*; *see* 11 U.S.C. § 350(b). Courts thus regard a case as fully administered when the plan has been substantially consummated and the matters that remain are ministerial or are governed by the plan and can be carried out by the reorganized debtor without court supervision. *See In re Kliegl Bros. Universal Elec. Stage Lighting Co.*, 238 B.R. 531, 542 (Bankr. E.D.N.Y. 1999); *In re Federated Dep’t Stores, Inc.*, 43 F. App’x 820, 822–23 (6th Cir. 2002). [Cite-check; add controlling Ninth Circuit/District of Oregon authority if available.]")

2\. A small number of discrete, ministerial items remain, and the Reorganized Debtor discloses each of them candidly in Part II.E below: (a) the Court's ruling on the pending motion to approve the \$525,000 settlement of the sole remaining adversary proceeding \[Dkt. No. 498\], which is set for hearing on February 20, 2025, and the receipt and distribution of the resulting net proceeds to Class 4; (b) payment of the U.S. Trustee quarterly fees for the first quarter of 2025 and for the quarter in which the case is closed; (c) filing of the January 2025 and subsequent post-confirmation operating reports, including a final report through the closing date; (d) \[final allowance of the remaining professional and Plan Administrator compensation for the pre-closing period;\] and (e) filing of a supplemental final report by the Plan Administrator and written confirmation that IRS Claim No. 14 has been satisfied. None of these items requires continued estate administration of the type that justifies keeping a chapter 11 case open.

3\. Consistent with the Region 18 U.S. Trustee's *Guidelines for Motions Seeking Entry of Final Decree in Chapter 11 Cases* (rev. Jan. 2024) (the "**UST Guidelines**"), which expressly contemplate that a final decree may be conditioned on payment of outstanding quarterly fees and the Court's approval of a pending settlement, the Reorganized Debtor requests entry of a final decree that becomes effective upon the Reorganized Debtor's filing of a certification that each of the Closing Conditions (defined below) has been satisfied, absent timely objection by the U.S. Trustee. Keeping the case open beyond that point would serve only to impose continuing quarterly fees and reporting costs on the Reorganized Debtor without any corresponding benefit to creditors.

**I. JURISDICTION, VENUE, AND STATUTORY PREDICATES**

4\. The Court has jurisdiction over this Motion under 28 U.S.C. §§ 157 and 1334. This is a core proceeding under 28 U.S.C. § 157(b)(2)(A) and (O). Venue is proper under 28 U.S.C. §§ 1408 and 1409.

5\. The Court expressly retained jurisdiction "to enter a final decree closing this case pursuant to 11 U.S.C. § 350(a) and Fed. R. Bankr. P. 3022." Confirmation Order ¶ O(n); *see also* Plan § 12.1(k).

6\. The statutory and rule predicates for the relief requested are section 350(a) of the Bankruptcy Code, Bankruptcy Rule 3022, and \[the applicable Local Bankruptcy Rules of this Court\].

**II. BACKGROUND**

**A. The Chapter 11 Case**

7\. The Debtor is an Oregon corporation (EIN 93-1284756) headquartered at 4200 Evergreen Industrial Parkway, Suite 300, Medford, Oregon 97501. It is a vertically integrated timber harvesting, sawmill, and engineered wood products company with six sawmill and processing facilities in Oregon and Washington and harvesting rights on approximately 340,000 acres of managed timberland. Before the petition it employed approximately 1,400 people and generated annual revenue of approximately \$185 million.

8\. On March 14, 2022 (the "**Petition Date**"), the Debtor filed a voluntary petition for relief under chapter 11 of the Bankruptcy Code \[Dkt. No. 1\]. The Debtor's schedules reflected assets of approximately \$198.6 million and liabilities of approximately \$247.3 million. No trustee or examiner was appointed. The Debtor operated its business and managed its property as a debtor in possession under sections 1107(a) and 1108 of the Bankruptcy Code until the Effective Date.

9\. On April 8, 2022, the U.S. Trustee appointed the Official Committee of Unsecured Creditors (the "**Committee**") \[Dkt. No. \[28/38\]\], which retained Pendergrass & Hale LLP as counsel \[Dkt. No. 42\]. The Court approved the Debtor's retention of Ridgeline & Sutter LLP as counsel \[Dkt. No. 12\] and Greenvale Consulting, Inc. ("**Greenvale**") as financial advisor and investment banker \[Dkt. No. 15\].

10\. The Court established August 1, 2022 as the general claims bar date and September 14, 2022 as the governmental bar date \[Dkt. No. 78\]. Approximately 312 proofs of claim were filed by the general bar date.

**B. The Plan and the Confirmation Order**

11\. Following a marketing process conducted by Greenvale, the Debtor selected Bramblecrest Capital Partners, LLC (the "**Plan Sponsor**") as plan sponsor \[Dkt. No. 175\]. The Debtor and the Plan Sponsor filed the Plan on September 22, 2023 \[Dkt. No. 398\]. \[The Court approved the disclosure statement by order entered \[[\_\_\], 2023 \[Dkt. No. \[]{.underline}\_\]\].\] Classes 2, 3, and 4 voted to accept the Plan; Class 5 was deemed to reject \[Dkt. No. 310\].

12\. After a four-day confirmation hearing held November 6--9, 2023, the Court entered the Confirmation Order on November 9, 2023 \[Dkt. No. 412\]. Notice of entry was served on November 10, 2023 \[Dkt. No. 415\]. The Confirmation Order was effective immediately upon entry, without the stay otherwise provided by Bankruptcy Rule 3020(e). Confirmation Order ¶ P. No appeal or motion for reconsideration of the Confirmation Order was filed, and the time to do so has long expired. \[Confirm against docket.\]

13\. The Plan classified claims and interests into five classes and provided the following treatment (Confirmation Order ¶ D; Plan Art. III):

Emmerich, with authority to make Class 4 distributions, resolve disputed claims, prosecute Avoidance Actions, and wind down the estate. Confirmation Order ¶ H; Plan § 7.2. **C. The Effective Date and Substantial Consummation**

15\. All conditions precedent to the Effective Date were satisfied, and the Effective Date occurred on December 1, 2023 \[Dkt. No. 420\]. On that date: (a) the Plan Sponsor funded its \$38,500,000 new value contribution; (b) the \$55,000,000 asset-based revolving exit facility with Timberline National Bank, N.A. 3\. **Closing Certification.** Within seven (7) days after the Closing Conditions have been satisfied, the Reorganized Debtor shall file, and serve on the United States Trustee and all parties that have requested notice under Fed. R. Bankr. P. 2002, a certification (the "**Closing Certification**") stating that each Closing Condition has been satisfied and identifying, by docket number or attached exhibit, the evidence of satisfaction of each Closing Condition.

4\. **U.S. Trustee Review; Closing Date.** The United States Trustee may file an objection to the Closing Certification, limited to whether the Closing Conditions have been satisfied, within fourteen (14) days after service of the Closing Certification. If no such objection is timely filed, or upon the withdrawal or resolution of any such objection by the Court, this Final Decree shall become effective, and the Clerk of the Court is directed to close the Chapter 11 Case, without further notice, hearing, or order of the Court (the date on which the Chapter 11 Case is closed, the "**Closing Date**"). The Clerk is further directed to close Adversary Proceeding No. 22-03091-PCW upon the filing of the dismissal referenced in paragraph 2(a), to the extent not already closed.

5\. **Outside Date.** If the Closing Certification has not been filed by \[June 30, 2025\], the Reorganized Debtor shall file a status report describing the status of each unsatisfied Closing Condition and the anticipated date of satisfaction, and the Court may set a further hearing.

6\. **Quarterly Fees and Reports.** Until the Closing Date, the Reorganized Debtor shall continue to (a) pay quarterly fees under 28 U.S.C. § 1930(a)(6) when due and (b) file monthly post-confirmation operating reports in the form required by the United States Trustee. The Reorganized Debtor's obligation to pay quarterly fees accrued through the Closing Date shall survive entry of this Final Decree and the closing of the Chapter 11 Case. The Reorganized Debtor shall pay the quarterly fee for the quarter in which the Closing Date occurs, calculated on disbursements through the Closing Date, no later than \[the date such fee is due under 28 U.S.C. § 1930(a)(6) / ten (10) days after the Closing Date\]. After the Closing Date, no further quarterly fees shall accrue and no further operating reports shall be required, unless the Chapter 11 Case is reopened.

7\. **Plan Administrator.** Compensation and reimbursement of expenses of the Plan Administrator for services rendered after the Closing Date shall be paid by the Reorganized Debtor in the ordinary course, without further application to or order of this Court, in accordance with Confirmation Order ¶ H and Plan § 7.2(d). The Plan Administrator's appointment shall continue after the Closing Date solely to the extent provided in the Plan and the Confirmation Order and shall terminate in accordance with Plan § 7.4.

8\. **Survival of Discharge, Injunctions, and Plan Provisions.** Nothing in this Final Decree or the closing of the Chapter 11 Case shall modify, impair, or otherwise affect the Plan, the Confirmation Order, or any agreement, instrument, or document executed or delivered in connection therewith, including the Exit Facility documents, the New Senior Secured Notes, and the New Subordinated Secured Notes. Without limiting the foregoing, the discharge granted under 11 U.S.C. § 1141(d) and Confirmation Order ¶ K; the permanent injunction set forth in Confirmation Order ¶ L and Plan § 10.2; the injunction arising under 11 U.S.C. § 524; and the exculpation and other provisions identified in Plan § 12.6 shall survive entry of this Final Decree and the closing of the Chapter 11 Case and shall remain in full force and effect.

9\. **Retention of Jurisdiction.** Notwithstanding entry of this Final Decree and the closing of the Chapter 11 Case, the Court shall retain jurisdiction to the fullest extent provided in Confirmation Order ¶ O and Plan § 12.1, including, without limitation, jurisdiction to (a) enforce and interpret the Plan, the Confirmation Order, and this Final Decree; (b) hear and determine any dispute arising under or related to the Plan or the Confirmation Order, including disputes regarding distributions and the Plan Administrator's duties, powers, and compensation; (c) enforce the discharge and injunctions referenced in paragraph 8; and (d) hear and determine any motion to reopen the Chapter 11 Case under 11 U.S.C. § 350(b).

10\. **Reopening.** Entry of this Final Decree is without prejudice to the right of the Reorganized Debtor, the United States Trustee, or any other party in interest to seek to reopen the Chapter 11 Case for cause pursuant to 11 U.S.C. § 350(b) and Fed. R. Bankr. P. 5010.

11\. **Implementation.** The Reorganized Debtor and the Plan Administrator are authorized to take all actions necessary or appropriate to implement this Final Decree. The Reorganized Debtor shall serve this Final Decree within three (3) business days after its entry on the United States Trustee and all parties served with the Motion, and shall serve notice of the Closing Date on the same parties within three (3) business days after the Closing Date.

12\. **Immediate Effect.** Except as provided in paragraphs 2 through 4 with respect to the effectiveness of the closing of the Chapter 11 Case, this Final Decree shall be effective and enforceable immediately upon entry.

I drafted both documents, but the case can't honestly be certified as "fully administered" yet. So the motion asks for a conditional final decree: the case closes only after a set of closing conditions are met and certified to the U.S. Trustee, and the proposed order matches that. Both files open and pass the docx validation script.

Files in /workspace/output:
- /workspace/output/motion-for-final-decree.docx
- /workspace/output/proposed-order-final-decree.docx

**Why it has to be conditional.** On the current record several items are still open:
- **Pacific Rim settlement:** the $525,000 settlement motion (Dkt. 498) isn't heard until Feb. 20, 2025. The adversary proceeding is still pending and the proceeds haven't been paid out to Class 4.
- **U.S. Trustee fees:** the Q1 2025 fee (about $10,400) hasn't been paid, and a fee will also be due for the quarter the case closes.
- **January 2025 operating report:** not yet filed; it's due Feb. 20, 2025.
- **Plan Administrator report:** the Final Status Report (Dkt. 501) needs a supplement. It's dated Jan. 31 but reports Feb. 3 and Feb. 5 events as already done, and it doesn't cover the Pacific Rim money.

The proposed order lists these as closing conditions. The Reorganized Debtor files a certification once they're met, the U.S. Trustee gets 14 days to object, and an outside date triggers a status report. It also keeps the discharge and injunctions in force, preserves the Court's retained jurisdiction and reopening under § 350(b), and lets Plan Administrator fees after closing be paid without court approval.

**What the motion contains.** It tracks the Region 18 U.S. Trustee guidelines: background, the legal standard, an argument on each factor, and the seven required certifications. It also has a reconciliation of the distributions (Exhibit A), a Plan Administrator support block and a certificate of service.

**Drafter's notes.** The motion opens with a page of notes to you, marked privileged, which must be removed before filing. The main points:
- **IRS Claim No. 14 doesn't add up.** Five "annual" payments supposedly finished Aug. 15, 2024, and the notice of payment (Dkt. 464) was filed three days before that date. The figures total only the $1,287,450 face amount with no interest: 5 × $214,575 = $1,072,875, against the full claim. I described the payments factually and made written IRS confirmation a closing condition.
- **Our firm's final fee application isn't on the docket.** The summary calls the $4.85M "final," but the docket shows only an interim application (Dkt. 440) and an interim order (Dkt. 450).
- **Plan Administrator pay needs court approval.** Confirmation Order ¶ H requires approval of its pay for work before the decree, which conflicts with the plan summary. Only an interim application through Mar. 31, 2024 has been approved.
- **The source documents contradict each other on docket numbers and facts.**
  - The Plan is cited as Dkt. 398, 387 and 268.
  - The disclosure statement, committee appointment and Clearwater objection numbers also differ between documents.
  - The prepetition notes appear as 9.25% due 2024 in one place and 9.75% due 2025 in another.
  - The financial advisor is named as both Northstar and Greenvale.

  I used neutral terms and bracketed the uncertain numbers; they all need checking against the actual court docket.
- **Aggregate distribution figure corrected.** The Plan Administrator's $112.69M total wrongly counts the $2,237,500 reserve surplus returned to the Reorganized Debtor. Creditors actually received $110,449,950.
- **Not yet confirmed:** tax-return status (no source document addresses it), the Q4 2024 fee payment date and amount, final orders on the five disputed claims, and how the Pacific Rim proceeds are split among Class 4 holders.

Bracketed placeholders remain for dates, docket numbers, the local rules, service addresses and the supporting declarations. All case citations need a cite-check.
